metrics.method: Full history 2026-03-23 to 2026-09-25, 890 messages (466 Vale / 424 our side, per config/clients.yaml client_aliases=[Vale]; all other senders are team.yaml staff). client_questions_total = Vale messages containing '?' (58); multi-message bursts merged would give ~70 distinct asks, so 58 is a floor. unanswered_over_24h = manual read of all 58: 9 never substantively answered (Jul 28 'Is there a way to check what's missing?', Jul 28 'Should I change my password?', Aug 3 'John we can do Friday?', Aug 3 live-prep pair, Aug 3 'I have more lives to schedule', Aug 7 'Was a call booked for today?', Aug 7 fan-notes request, Sep 10 'What's its for?'/which Snapchat, Sep 25 'so just have to wait?') plus 4 answered only after 24h (Mar 29, Jun 29, Jul 6, Aug 18). Automated thread-aware proximity scoring gives 7, which overcounts as answered any reply that lands in the same topic without addressing the question. Response lag measured on 118 client bursts (>1h apart): median 34 minutes, p90 21.3h, max 115h; 9 bursts waited >24h for any team reply. max_team_silence_days = longest gap between consecutive team messages across the whole log (5.2d, 2026-05-05 to 2026-05-10; matched by 4.9d 2026-09-17 to 2026-09-22 while her IG was restricted); the account lead alone has been silent 10 days at window close and Derrek 55. Promises = explicit dated commitments by our side read out of the transcript (e.g. 'I'll send X in the morning', 'we can get them scheduled this week', a delivery implied by money collected); kept = evidence of delivery in-chat; lapsed = no evidence and now overdue.

top_fix: Give this account one named owner and a written commitment ledger they read out to her once a week: every paid fan order (fan, amount, date sold, delivery status), every promise we have made with a date and an owner, and every open client question — with a standing rule that nothing gets closed until it is confirmed back to her in writing. Every severe gap on this account is the same failure wearing different clothes: ~$5,300 of fan money and 27 lapsed promises went stale not because anyone refused, but because no single person was accountable for the list and nobody was ever obliged to report on it. A weekly five-minute read-out would have surfaced Tyler's $700 custom in April instead of never, caught John's $2,000 order four months before we found it by accident, forced the girl-girl vault purge and the sexting template to close, made Michelle's stopped leak report and three unreconciled payments visible the week they happened, and — most importantly — put a human being in front of a client who has quietly stopped asking us for anything.
